app.title: Jak Level Editor
menu.file.extract.tip: Reads the levels of %s from your disc into the library, once.
menu.file.extract.wip_tip: Extracting the levels of %s is planned, with their editing: not available yet.
menu.edit.create_prefab: Create a prefab from the selection...
menu.view.game_view.tip: The level drawn by the game's own renderer, as the game would show it once exported: its lighting at the hour chosen (the sun, the ambient light, the lamps), its fog, its ways of drawing. On from the start; changes show at once. Key: G.
menu.view.game_view.unavailable: The game's renderer is not available: %s
menu.view.game_lights.tip: The lights baked in the level (palettes 5 to 7): its lamps at night, the lights always on, the flickering ones, as the city's levels drive them.
menu.view.effects.tip: The particles of the level's effects (steam, sparks, smoke, fire, lights), launched and moved by the game's own rules and drawn with its textures.
menu.view.select_terrain.tip: The large flat pieces of the levels (their ground) are locked so that clicks go to what stands on them. Check this to select them too.
menu.game.tip: The game whose levels you edit and export: Jak 3 for now.
menu.game.wip_tip: Editing the levels of %s and exporting them for it is planned, not available yet.
toolbar.snap.steps.tip: The steps of the snap: 0.5 m, 15 degrees... (modular building: walls of 4 m on a grid of 0.5 m)
toolbar.snap.keys: While dragging: Ctrl snaps (or not), Shift is ten times finer.
toolbar.paste.tip: Paste the copied elements where they were (Ctrl+V), then move them.
levels.no_library: Jak 3 is not extracted yet. The editor reads the levels of your own copy of Jak 3: extract them first from your disc (.iso file or folder).
levels.folder_empty: Jak 3 is not extracted in this folder:
levels.with_actors.tip: Loads the level (or adds it) with its actors: crates, doors, effects... Unchecked: its decor alone, but the platforms and bridges it needs to be crossed stay. Creatures never come.
levels.add.tip: Adds this level to the document, at its place in the game's world: levels side by side in the game meet here too. The levels the game shows with it and its mission layers come with it.
levels.add.in_document: This level is already in the document
levels.add.no_document: Open a level or start a new one before adding %s
levels.add.busy: A level is loading: wait before adding %s
levels.remove.not_added: Only a level added to the document can be removed
story.enabled.tip: Shows the level as the game shows it at this point of the story: the actors, decor and mission layers of that moment. Unchecked: every state of the level at once.
story.level.tip: The level shown by the bar: each level of the document has its own point of the story
story.slider.none: This level does not change along the story
story.no_change: The same all along the story
story.slider.tip: The states of this level along the story: the start of the game, then each step of the missions that changes it (the steps that change nothing here are skipped).
story.all: Every state of the level at once
catalog.no_library: The catalog lists the objects of the game: extract it first.
catalog.models.jak2.tip: Jak II's objects and props, by their model: placed as decor (their textures renamed, lit like the level around them). Their behavior is Jak II's code, which Jak 3 does not have.
catalog.my_models.tip: Your own model, imported from Blender or another program (File > Import a model, or the file dropped on the window): kept in the library's models/ folder.
catalog.model_tip: Placed as decor: the game draws it but it does nothing.
catalog.no_model: The game draws it without a model (effects, lights): a marker in the editor
catalog.effect_tip: A particle effect of the game (steam, sparks, smoke, lights...): its particles as the game makes them, in the picture and in the level.
catalog.indexing: Reading the decor of the levels: %d / %d (once)
catalog.empty: No object with a model in the extracted levels.
catalog.not_found: In no extracted level: placed with default data
catalog.place_tip: Click it, then click in the view to place it (R turns it), or drag it into the view.
catalog.decor.failed: The decor of this level cannot be read (see the log).
catalog.decor.none: No decor to reuse in this level. Levels extracted before this version have no pieces: extract the game again.
catalog.prototype: Decor prototype, %d copies in its level
prefabs.no_library: Prefabs are kept with the extracted game. Extract a game and load one of its levels first.
prefabs.create: Create a prefab from the selection
prefabs.create.tip: Select elements in the level (Shift + click adds one), then save them together as a prefab.
prefabs.empty: No prefab yet. Select elements of the level, then Create a prefab.
prefabs.cell_tip: Click: place copies where you click - drag into the view: place one
prefabs.game.making: Making the game's prefabs from your levels: %d / %d
prefabs.game.make: Make all the game's prefabs now (%zu left)
prefabs.game.make.tip: They are made level by level when the panel shows them (each level read once, a few seconds) and saved with your prefabs (prefabs/game/). This makes all the others now: under a minute and 0.4 GB.
inspector.title: Inspector
inspector.no_level: No level loaded. Choose one in the Levels panel, then Load the level.
inspector.companions.tip: A level the game shows with this one. Uncheck to hide it.
inspector.added_levels.main.tip: The level opened: click to frame it
inspector.added_levels.junction.tip: Frame where this level meets the level opened
inspector.added_levels.select.tip: Selects the whole level (Ctrl+L from one of its elements), to move, turn or scale it with the gizmo
inspector.neighbors.tip: A level the game displays with one of the document's: click to add it, at its place
replace.title: Replace a level of the game
replace.none_chosen: None: a level of its own
replace.show.tip: Adds the game's level as it is, washed in blue: it is not selected, not exported, and shows where your level must meet the levels around it.
replace.shown.tip: Show or hide the game's level (blue)
replace.align: Place it where the original is
replace.align.tip: Moves your whole level (not the levels added next to it) so that its middle and its bottom are where %s's are. Then turn it, or move it with the gizmo (Select).
replace.align.disabled: Show the original first: your level is placed where %s is.
replace.turn.tip: Turns your whole level a quarter turn around its middle.
replace.select.tip: Selects your whole level: the gizmo moves and turns it (Snap: by steps; Shift: finer).
replace.continues: Where the game starts the player in %s:
replace.continues.tip: The continue points of the level replaced: the game puts the player there (a new game, a mission, a death). Green: your level has ground under it; orange: nothing within a few meters, the player would fall.
replace.continue.none: No ground under it within a few meters: build some, or move the level.
replace.export.tip: Level > Export for the game, set to replace this level of the game.
replace.none: Choose the level of the game it replaces first.
replace.show_first: Show the original (%s) first: your level is placed where it is.
replace.empty: Nothing to place: the document's own level is empty (%s).
inspector.layers: %zu mission layers, %zu shown at this point of the story
inspector.layers.tip: Layers are the actors some missions add to this level. The story bar shows those of the missions under way.
inspector.hint: Click an element of the level to select it. Shift + click adds to the selection.
inspector.scale.uniform.tip: Changing one value of the scale changes the three by the same ratio. Uncheck it to stretch along one axis.
inspector.locked.tip: A locked element is not selected by a click: clicks go to what stands on it. View > Select the ground selects the locked elements again.
import.title: From Jak II (%s)
import.tip: A structure of Jak II brought into this Jak 3 level: what was checked and converted when it came in.
import.check.mesh: Mesh: %zu triangles, %zu indices out of range, %zu textured pieces without texture coordinates
import.check.colors: Vertex colors (the game's lighting): %zu pieces without them, %zu values out of range
import.check.lighting: Lighting: %.2f times as bright as the Jak 3 decor of the level
import.check.materials: Materials: %zu, %zu blended (written cut out for the game, as Jak 3's)
import.check.textures: Textures: %zu, %zu renamed jak2-... (Jak 3 has an image of that name), %zu not a power of two up to 256
import.check.metadata: Data: no actor, no story, no collision of its own (made from its shape for the game), same units and axes as Jak 3
import.match_lighting.tip: Scales its vertex colors so that it is as bright as the Jak 3 decor of the level.
import.user.title: Imported model (%s)
import.check.user_mesh_uv: Mesh: %zu triangles; %zu pieces have an image but no UV map: they show one color (unwrap them in Blender)
import.check.size: Size: %.1f x %.1f x %.1f m (in Blender, 1 unit is 1 meter)
import.check.user_textures: Images: %zu, the largest %d pixels (over 1024, the level gets heavy)
import.check.plain: Colors without an image: %zu, made into small images (the game draws a material without one as a checkerboard)
import.check.parts: Parts: %zu (Blender's objects), placed as one piece
import.check.animations: Animations: %zu, a skeleton of %zu bones: played by the Preview below; in the game it stays still (decor)
import.check.collision: Collision: from its shape, %zu triangles (about %.0f around Jak at once; the game gathers 460)
import.check.collision_box: Collision: %zu triangles, about %.0f around Jak at once where the game gathers 460: he would fall through it, so it collides by the box around it (In the game > Its collision)
decor.title: In the game
decor.collision.game: Yes by default: the game's own collision there (exact).
decor.collision.shape: Yes by default: made from its shape by the level builder.
decor.collision.small: No by default: a small piece (under 4 m), as most of the game's details. Tick it for Jak to bump into it.
decor.collision.see_through: No by default: a surface seen through (water, glass).
decor.collision.on: Jak stands on it and bumps into it.
decor.collision.invisible_on: Not drawn in the game: only its collision is there (an invisible wall).
decor.invisible: Invisible in the game (an invisible wall)
decor.invisible.tip: Not drawn in the game, it still collides: a barrier at the edge of the level, a floor under a hole. The editor shows it.
decor.collision.box_on: Jak stands on the box around it and bumps into it (the box is not drawn).
decor.shape.tip: Its shape: exact, as many triangles as the model. The box around it: 12 triangles, for a detailed model (made in Blender, a statue) that Jak would fall through: the game gathers only about 460 triangles around him.
decor.shape.shape.tip: Exact: Jak walks on it and into its hollows, as many triangles as the model.
decor.shape.box.tip: 12 triangles, solid all around: Jak never falls through it, nor gets into its hollows.
decor.material: Ground material (the sound of the steps)
decor.material.group.sound: The sound of the steps and their dust
decor.material.stone.tip: Jak's steps, rolls and landings sound like stone.
decor.material.metal.tip: The sound of steps on metal: floors and catwalks of the city.
decor.material.wood.tip: The sound of steps on wood planks.
decor.material.grass.tip: The sound of steps in the grass.
decor.material.dirt.tip: The sound of steps on earth, and its dust.
decor.material.sand.tip: The sound of steps in the sand of the desert, and its dust.
decor.material.snow.tip: The sound of steps in the snow.
decor.material.deepsnow.tip: The sound of steps in deep snow.
decor.material.straw.tip: The sound of steps on straw.
decor.material.crwood.tip: The sound of the wood of a crate.
decor.material.pcmetal.tip: The sound of the Precursors' metal.
decor.material.hotcoals.tip: The sound of steps on embers (they do not burn: see Effect on Jak).
decor.material.lava.tip: The sound of lava (it does not burn by itself: see Effect on Jak).
decor.material.tar.tip: The sound of steps in tar.
decor.material.swamp.tip: The sound of steps in a swamp.
decor.material.rotate.tip: A surface of the game's turning platforms: their sound.
decor.material.ice.tip: Jak slides on it: he walks as on ice and keeps his speed.
decor.material.gravel.tip: Loose ground: Jak slides down its slopes.
decor.material.quicksand.tip: Jak gets bogged down: he moves at half his speed and turns slowly.
decor.material.tube.tip: Jak cannot walk on it: he slides off (pipes, rounded tops).
decor.material.waterbottom.tip: The bottom of water: Jak is in the water there (and can drown).
decor.material.stopproj.tip: The shots of the guns stop on it.
decor.event.deadlyup: Hurts him and throws him up
decor.event.burnup: Burns him and throws him up
decor.event.none.tip: Nothing: Jak stands on it and walks on it as on any ground.
decor.event.deadly.tip: Jak loses health and is pushed back each time he touches it (spikes, barbed wire).
decor.event.burn.tip: Jak burns: he loses health (fire, embers).
decor.event.deadlyup.tip: Jak loses health and is thrown up in the air.
decor.event.burnup.tip: As the game's lava: Jak burns and jumps up in the air.
decor.event.endlessfall.tip: Jak falls without end, then starts again at the last continue point (the void under a level).
decor.event.melt.tip: Jak dies at once (melts), then starts again at the last continue point.
decor.mode.auto.tip: Its slope decides: the steep faces are walls, the others ground.
decor.mode.ground.tip: Jak walks on it, whatever its slope.
decor.mode.wall.tip: Jak slides along it and cannot stand on it.
decor.mode.obstacle.tip: It stops Jak, as a wall, but creatures do not walk on it.
decor.mode.tip: Ground (Jak walks on it), wall (he slides along it) or obstacle. By default its slope decides: the level builder makes walls of the steep faces.
decor.flag.noedge: Jak cannot hang from its edges
decor.flag.noedge.tip: Its edges are not ledges to grab.
decor.flag.nocamera.tip: The camera does not stop against it (thin decor near the path).
decor.flag.nolineofsight.tip: The enemies see Jak through it.
collision.title: Collision
collision.help: What Jak stands on and bumps into, a color per surface. Click a face; Shift + click adds it or takes it out; a double click picks the faces of its surface touching it; drag a box for every face whose middle is in it. Every change can be undone.
collision.legend.tip: The surfaces of the collision shown and their faces. Click one to pick all its faces (Shift: add them).
collision.paint: Give it to the faces picked
collision.no_point: Click where it goes first: the yellow cross.
collision.add.tip: Of the surface chosen above, its base on the yellow cross: a floor over a hole, an invisible wall at the edge of the level, a step. Width, height, depth in meters.
collision.from_pieces: Collision from the shape of the %zu pieces selected
collision.from_pieces.tip: The pieces selected before the tool get faces of collision of their shape, of the surface chosen, to change one by one here; their own collision becomes none.
collision.check.found: %zu places (in red): more triangles there than the game gathers around Jak at once (460).
collision.check.none: None: nowhere does Jak meet more than the game gathers at once.
collision.check.tip: The floors of the collision shown where Jak, standing, meets more triangles than the game gathers around him: he falls through the floor there. Delete faces there, or give the pieces a simpler collision.
decor.launch.values.tip: Jak lands `distance` meters away along the element's facing turned by `direction`, `landing height` above its top.
inspector.scale.actor: The game ignores the scale of most objects: scale the decor (pieces, parts, models), or check the object in the game.
inspector.shape.size.tip: Width, height and depth in meters. The texture repeats instead of stretching.
inspector.shape.tile.tip: Meters of the shape covered by one repeat of its texture.
inspector.shape.opening.tip: Width and height of the door or the window, in meters (a door from the ground, a window in the middle of the wall).
inspector.shape.apply_scale.tip: The scale stretches the texture: turned into the size, the texture repeats again.
inspector.material.image.tip: An image file (PNG, JPG, TGA, BMP) as its texture, for the selected elements drawing this material. It goes into the project and into the level exported for the game.
inspector.material.textures.tip: Choose its texture among the games' textures: the game (Jak 3, Jak II), a level that uses it, a part of its name.
textures.title: Game textures
textures.level.tip: The textures a level's decor draws, those of every level, or those already in the document (the levels opened, the images added).
textures.filter: Search by name (e.g. wall, metal, wood)
textures.none: No texture: search for another name, or another level.
inspector.placing.help: Click in the view to place it: it is then selected (all of a prefab), the gizmo on it, to move it again at once; hold Shift when you let go of the button to go on placing copies. Keep the left button down and move the mouse: left and right, up and down move it (Ctrl: forward and back instead of up and down, Shift finer); it is placed when you let go. Hold the right button and move the mouse to turn it on every axis; R or Ctrl + wheel turns it around the vertical. Esc stops.
status.select: Click: select - Right button: fly (on the selection: turn it) - W / E / R: move / rotate / scale - F: frame
status.place: Click: place (Shift: keep placing) - Left button held: move it left / right, up / down (Ctrl: forward / back) - Right button held: turn it on every axis - R / Ctrl + wheel: turn - Esc: stop
status.remote.tip: An assistant is connected through the MCP server: its changes appear here and can be undone.
viewport.hint.extract: Start with File > Extract game assets
viewport.hint.load: Choose a level in the Levels panel, then Load the level
viewport.hint.camera: Right button + WASD (ZQSD on AZERTY): fly
help.camera.1: Right button + WASD (ZQSD on AZERTY): fly; Q / E (A / E on AZERTY): down / up. On the selection, the right button turns it instead
help.camera.2: Shift: faster, Ctrl: slower; the wheel while flying changes the speed
help.camera.3: Wheel: forward; middle button: pan; Alt + left button: turn around
help.camera.4: F: frame the selection; Home: frame the level
help.story.1: Levels open without their creatures (enemies, characters, the Titan suit) and without the invisible logic actors.
help.story.2: The bar at the bottom of the view shows a level at a point of the game: its slider goes through the states of the level (the start, then each step that changes it); with several levels, choose which one in its list.
help.story.3: Uncheck Story to see every state of the level at once. View > Ocean shows or hides the sea, View > Fog the haze over distant backdrop scenery.
help.editing.1: Click: select; Shift or Ctrl + click: add to the selection; drag: box selection
help.editing.2: W / E / R: move / rotate / scale (an axis stretches, the center grows or shrinks). While dragging: Shift is ten times finer, Ctrl snaps; the value is written next to the cursor
help.editing.10: Right button held on the selection, or on what you are placing: turns it on every axis with the mouse
help.editing.3: Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V: copy / paste in place; Ctrl+D: duplicate; Del: delete
help.editing.5: The ground is locked: clicks go to what stands on it (View > Select the ground). Click again at the same place to select what is behind or under the selection

extract.title: Extract game assets
extract.intro: The editor reads the levels of your own copy of the game: the image (.iso) of your disc, or the folder of a disc already extracted (for example iso_data/jak3 of OpenGOAL). Nothing from the game comes with the editor.
extract.missing: ogle-extract is not next to the editor.
extract.missing.help: It is built from extractor/ (CMake), then put with its ogle-extract-data/ folder in one of these folders; or the environment variable JLE_EXTRACTOR gives its path:
extract.jak1: Jak and Daxter is recognized, but its levels are not extracted yet: editing them is planned.
extract.wrong_game: This disc is neither Jak 3 nor Jak II: choose another disc.
extract.jak2: Jak II: its levels are extracted next to Jak 3's (to jak2/), to bring their structures (buildings, the palace, pillars, cables) into your Jak 3 levels: Catalog > Decor > Jak II.
extract.disc.choose: Choose the .iso file or the folder of your %s disc.
extract.not_recognized: ogle-extract does not recognize this disc
extract.destination.where: The levels go to %s/%s/, one folder per level
extract.stopped: ogle-extract stopped before the end (see its log)
extract.done: Done in %s: %zu levels. Load one in the Levels panel.
extract.error.not_found: Neither an .iso file nor a folder
extract.error.not_jak: No DGO folder: not a Jak disc
extract.error.not_jak3: Neither a Jak 3 nor a Jak II disc
extract.error.no_executable: The game's executable (SCUS_..., SCES_...) is not on the disc
extract.fetch.help: This application can download it for you (about 30 MB).
extract.host_disc: The disc your OpenGOAL installation already extracted.
welcome.title: Welcome to Jak Level Editor
welcome.intro: Before you start, choose where the editor keeps your library: everything it makes from your copy of the game, and everything you make with it.
welcome.holds.games: the levels extracted from your Jak 3 disc (and from Jak II's, for its buildings): about 4 GB
welcome.holds.exports: your levels exported for the game
welcome.default_game: This folder already holds an extracted game: you can start right away.
welcome.next_extract: Next step: extract the levels of your Jak 3 disc into it (File > Extract game assets).
welcome.later: You can change it later in File > Settings.
settings.title: Settings
settings.library.help: The folder of the extracted game (jak3/, jak2/), your projects (projects/), your exports (exports/) and your prefabs (prefabricated/).
settings.library.game: An extracted game is in this folder.
settings.library.no_game: No extracted game in this folder yet.
settings.library.empty: The editor now uses this folder; nothing was moved or deleted in %s. Extract the game there (File > Extract game assets), or copy the old folder's content into it by hand.
settings.library.none: Choose a folder for the library.
settings.extractor.missing: Missing. It is looked for in:
settings.remote.help: An AI assistant such as Claude can build levels with the editor through its MCP server (jak-level-editor-mcp, on this computer). It reaches the editor with a key the editor writes into its settings folder (remote.json) when it listens: nothing else can control it.
settings.remote.allow: Let an assistant control the editor
settings.remote.listening: Listening on port %d of this computer.
settings.remote.session: The MCP server started the editor: it listens for this session.
menu.level.add: Add a level next to it...
menu.level.replace: Replace a level of the game...
menu.level.restore_effects.tip: Adds back the particle effects of the levels of the document as the game has them (steam, sparks, lights), where the document has none: a project made before the editor kept them, or effects deleted. Those whose decor was taken out of the level are left out. Undoable.
navmesh.title: Nav meshes
navmesh.help: Where the creatures of the level walk: the enemies and citizens of Jak 3 follow nav meshes. They are generated from the walkable surfaces of the decor shown (not the water, the glows nor the objects), kept where the creature has room, and cut to the game's limits: convex polygons of 3 or 4 corners, at most 255 per mesh, each mesh in one piece.
navmesh.radius.tip: How far the creature keeps from the walls: the nav mesh shrinks by this much.
navmesh.height.tip: The room the creature needs above the floor: floors under a lower ceiling are left out.
navmesh.climb.tip: The highest step between two floors the creature climbs.
navmesh.cell.tip: The finer, the closer the nav mesh follows the walls, and the longer it takes. Very large regions use coarser voxels.
navmesh.edge.tip: The longest polygon edge along the walls: longer edges, fewer polygons.
navmesh.error.tip: How far an outline may stray from the walls: more tolerance, fewer polygons.
navmesh.min_region.tip: Walkable islands smaller than this are left out (the tops of crates, ledges).
navmesh.keep_selected: Only the ground under the selection
navmesh.keep_selected.tip: Keeps only the pieces of walkable ground that the selected elements stand on (select something in a street, a yard): the roofs, ledges and closed rooms, where no creature goes, are left out.
navmesh.generate_all.tip: Replaces the nav meshes of the level.
navmesh.generate_selection.tip: Only around the selected elements: replaces the nav meshes there.
navmesh.last: Last generation: %zu nav meshes, %zu polygons in %.1f s
navmesh.split: %zu pieces of ground had more than 255 polygons: each was cut in several nav meshes (creatures do not go from one to another).
navmesh.left_out: %zu pieces of ground away from the selection were left out.
navmesh.bad: %zu of them do not suit the game (see the inspector)
navmesh.export.help: Writes the nav meshes as the game's levels hold them (entity-nav-mesh: polygons, route table, polygon grid) in a nav_data file (.json) for OpenGOAL's level builder (the "nav_data" of a level).
navmesh.first_id.tip: The entity id of the first nav mesh, the next ones follow: unique in the game and not an actor's.
export.title: Export for the game
export.help: Writes what the view shows as a custom level of OpenGOAL for Jak 3: the files its level builder takes. Hidden levels and elements are left out.
export.name: Name
export.name.tip: The level's name in the game (long_name): 3 to 10 lower case letters, digits or '-'. It must not be a level of the game.
export.nickname.tip: 3 letters: the name of its DGO file (XXX.DGO). It must not be another level's.
export.iso_name.tip: Up to 8 upper case letters or digits.
export.base_id.tip: The actors are numbered from it. Above the ids of the game's own actors, and apart from your other levels'.
export.actors.tip: The actors shown (crates, doors, effects...), with their data. Unchecked: the decor alone, but the platforms and bridges it needs to be crossed stay.
export.collision.game.tip: The levels' own collision, exact and light, where their decor is still in place; taken out where a piece was deleted, moved or hidden. The builder makes the rest from the shape of the decor (the elements placed or moved).
export.collision.decor.tip: The builder makes all the collision from the shape of the decor, with automatic walls. Far denser than the game's: where the decor is detailed, Jak can fall through the floor (the report says where).
export.start.tip: Where the player starts (the level's continue point), in meters.
export.start.reset.tip: A continue point of the level opened, else the ground at the middle of the document.
export.replaces.none: none: a level of its own
export.replaces.tip: A level of the game this one replaces: only the document's own level is written (not the levels added next to it), its DGO has that level's code, and level-info.gc gives the one line to change in the game's definition of that level (its nickname).
export.replaces.start: The player starts at the continue points of %s: the game keeps them.
export.folder_path.tip: The project's export: README.md (how to bring the level into the game), and the folders custom_assets and goal_src to copy into the jak-project checkout.

guide.title: Guide
guide.camera.title: Fly around
guide.camera.keys: Right button + WASD, wheel, F, Home
guide.camera.text: Hold the right button and fly with WASD (ZQSD on AZERTY), Q / E (A / E) down and up; Shift faster, Ctrl slower. The wheel moves forward, the middle button pans, Alt + left button turns around.
guide.camera.example: Example: select an airlock of the Industrial Zone, press F to fly to it, then Home to see the whole level again.
guide.select.title: Select
guide.select.text: Click an element to select it; Shift or Ctrl + click adds to the selection. The cursor tells what it points at (its name, its prefab or group) and outlines it. Double click, or hold the left button still on it, to select its whole prefab or group (else its assembly). Click again at the same place to reach what is behind or under it. The ground is locked, so that clicks go to what stands on it (View > Select the ground).
guide.select.example: Example: click a lamp post of a street, then Ctrl + click the bench next to it, to move both together.
guide.box_select.title: Box selection
guide.box_select.text: Drag a box over the view from an empty spot: what it would select is outlined as it grows and counted next to the cursor. Shift adds it to the selection, Ctrl takes it out. The ground and the levels shown to compare stay out of it. Dragging from an element already selected moves the selection instead.
guide.box_select.example: Example: frame the crates of a courtyard in one box and delete them at once.
guide.move.title: Move
guide.move.text: Drag an arrow of the gizmo to move along an axis, a square to move on a plane. The distance is shown by the cursor; Shift is ten times finer, Ctrl snaps to the grid.
guide.move.example: Example: lift a platform by 2 m (the green arrow), so that Jak needs a double jump to reach it.
guide.rotate.title: Rotate
guide.rotate.keys: E, right button on the selection
guide.rotate.text: Drag a ring of the gizmo to turn the selection around that axis; the angle is shown by the cursor. Or hold the right button on the selection (or on what you are placing) and move the mouse: it turns on every axis, across around the vertical and up and down around the camera's horizontal (Shift: finer). With Snap, by steps of 15 degrees (the arrow next to Snap changes them).
guide.rotate.example: Example: turn a bridge by 90 degrees so that it crosses the canal the other way.
guide.scale.title: Scale
guide.scale.text: Drag the square at the end of an axis to stretch along it, the square in the center to make the whole bigger or smaller. The inspector's Scale gives exact values (Keep the proportions).
guide.scale.example: Example: stretch a metal plate along X into a longer walkway between two roofs.
guide.snap.title: Snap to the grid
guide.snap.text: With Snap on, moves land on a grid (0.5 m), turns go by steps of 15 degrees and scales by steps of 0.1; the arrow next to it changes the steps. Ctrl while dragging snaps, or stops snapping, for one move.
guide.snap.example: Example: walls of 4 m moved on a grid of 0.5 m meet edge to edge, with no gap.
guide.local.title: Local axes
guide.local.text: The gizmo follows the selection's own axes, turned with it, instead of the world's: to slide along a turned catwalk or wall, to turn around its own axis.
guide.local.example: Example: a ramp turned by 30 degrees: in Local, its red arrow slides it along its own length.
guide.free_rotate.title: Free rotation
guide.free_rotate.keys: right button held on the selection
guide.free_rotate.text: Hold the right button on the selection, or on what you are placing, and move the mouse: it turns on every axis, left-right around the vertical, up-down around the camera's horizontal. Shift: finer; with Snap, by its steps of angle. Elsewhere the right button looks around.
guide.free_rotate.example: Example: tilt a fallen pillar so that it leans on a wall.
guide.game_view.title: Game rendering
guide.game_view.text: The level drawn by the game's own renderer, as the game will show it: its sky, its lighting at the hour and in the weather chosen (View > Sky, hour and weather...), its fog, its lamps at night. On from the start; every change shows at once. G switches to the editor's own view, every light of the level on.
guide.game_view.example: Example: set the hour to 21 h to see your street at night, its lamps lit.
guide.build.title: Build: shapes
guide.build.text: Blocks, floors, walls (with a door or a window), pillars, ramps, stairs, roofs and cylinders: click one, then click in the view to place it, again and again (Esc stops). The inspector changes its size: its texture repeats instead of stretching.
guide.build.example: Example: four walls of 4 m (one with a door) and a hip roof on top: a small house in a minute, snapped on the grid.
guide.palette.title: Materials of the games
guide.palette.text: Every texture of the games' levels: choose the game (Jak 3, or Jak II when it is extracted), a level (the textures its decor draws) or every level, and search by name. Select shapes or pieces of decor, then click a texture: they all take it (Ctrl+Z undoes it). In the inspector, Game textures... opens the same choice for one material of the selection.
guide.palette.example: Example: select the walls of your house, choose the level wascitya and pick a sandstone of Spargus: it fits in the desert.
guide.catalog.title: Catalog: objects
guide.catalog.text: The objects that make up a place: the game's props that only stand there (flags, windmills, a parked hellcat...), doors and airlocks, water, dark eco and lava. The particle effects have a category of their own (Effects). No creature, no collectible. Click one, then click in the view.
guide.catalog.example: Example: an airlock between your level and the next, steam over a vent, a neon sign over a shop.
guide.interactive.title: Catalog: interactive objects
guide.interactive.text: The objects that do something: crates, platforms and elevators, bouncers and board vents, buttons, breakable walls and fences, hazards. Their behavior is set in the inspector.
guide.interactive.example: Example: an elevator up to a rooftop, or a breakable fence hiding a shortcut.
guide.models.title: Catalog: models
guide.models.text: Every other model of the game but the characters: parts of objects, debris, props... placed as decor.
guide.models.example: Example: scatter debris and rubble around a wrecked tower.
guide.mymodels.title: My models (Blender)
guide.mymodels.text: Your own models, made in Blender or another program and exported as glTF (.glb, or .gltf with its files). Drop the file on the window, or File > Import a model: it is copied into the library (the catalog's Models, My models) and placed. The inspector says what was checked: its size, its images, its colors without an image (made into small images, which the game needs), its parts, its animations, its collision. Importing a file of the same name again replaces the model (edited in Blender).
guide.mymodels.example: Example: a market stall modeled in Blender, exported as stall.glb, dropped on the window, then placed again and again from My models.
guide.decor.title: Catalog: decor
guide.decor.text: The decor of the game's levels (their prototypes and the pieces of their shell), to reuse anywhere: search every level by name, or browse one.
guide.decor.example: Example: search 'pipe' to find the pipes of every level and lay them along your walls.
guide.jak2.title: Structures of Jak II
guide.jak2.text: The structures of Jak II (extracted from your Jak II disc with File > Extract game assets > Jak II): placed in a Jak 3 level, each is checked and converted (textures and names apart from Jak 3's, its lighting compared): see the inspector.
guide.jak2.example: Example: bring a pillar of Haven's palace, or its cables, into your Jak 3 level; Match the lighting if it looks too bright or too dark.
guide.prefab.title: Prefabs of your own
guide.prefab.text: Select elements, then Create a prefab: they are saved together, with their materials and behaviors, and appear in the Prefabs panel, to place again in any level.
guide.prefab.example: Example: a market stall made of crates, an awning and lamps, placed again in every street.
guide.game_prefabs.title: Prefabs of the game
guide.game_prefabs.text: Ready-made assemblies of Jak 3's decor, taken as the game put them: buildings, houses, bridges, platforms, vents, generators, industrial structures. They are made from your extracted levels (nothing of the game comes with the editor).
guide.game_prefabs.example: Example: a house of Spargus or a bridge of the Industrial Zone in one click, then change its pieces.
guide.bounce.title: Bounce
guide.bounce.text: Jak landing on its top bounces up, on foot and on the jetboard: the game's own bouncer, without a model of its own (the board vents of the Industrial Zone are made so), written in the level's code by the export.
guide.bounce.example: Example: a metal plate that throws Jak 8 m up, to reach a ledge.
guide.launch.title: Propulsion
guide.launch.text: Jak stepping on its top is thrown along an arc to a point you choose: the game's own launch (the Metal Head puffers'), written in the level's code by the export.
guide.launch.example: Example: a vent that sends Jak 20 m across a gap, onto the next roof.
guide.collision.title: Collision
guide.collision.text: Whether Jak stands on the element and bumps into it. By default it is what the game does: the game's own collision for the pieces of its levels where they are, none for the small pieces (under 4 m: pipes, lamps, decals) and the surfaces seen through (water, glass), else one made from its shape by the level builder. Tick or untick it to choose. In More options: an invisible wall (not drawn in the game, it still collides).
guide.collision.example: Example: untick it on a curtain of leaves so that Jak walks through it; tick it on a small crate he should climb.
guide.collision_tool.title: The collision tool
guide.collision_tool.text: C, or the toolbar's Collision: the levels' collision drawn over them, a color per surface (its material, its effect on Jak or its kind: ground, wall, obstacle). Pick faces (a click, Shift, a double click, a box, a surface of the legend, the faces under pieces) and give them another surface, delete them, move them, or add a floor or a box where you clicked. The export writes it with the level.
guide.collision_tool.example: Example: a lava floor of the volcano made stone so that Jak walks on it, and an invisible wall added at the edge of a cliff.
guide.ingame.title: In the game
guide.ingame.text: What the game does with an element of the decor, written by the export: its collision (whether Jak bumps into it), the material of its ground (the sound of his steps), its effect on Jak (hurts, burns, kills), and whether it makes him bounce or throws him somewhere. Each choice says what it does; the guide's tutorial In the game goes through them.
guide.ingame.example: Example: a lava floor: collision ticked, material Lava (its sound), effect Burns him and throws him up.
guide.surface.title: Ground material
guide.surface.text: What Jak walks on, as the game's surfaces have it: mostly the sound of his steps, rolls and landings, and the dust they raise (stone, metal, wood, sand, snow...). A few change how he moves: ice (he slides), gravel (he slides down slopes), quicksand (he gets bogged down), tube (he cannot walk on it), the bottom of water (he is in water). Stop shots: the guns' shots stop on it. Only with a collision.
guide.surface.example: Example: Metal for a catwalk (its clang), Ice for a frozen slope Jak slides down.
guide.event.title: Effect on Jak
guide.event.text: What touching the element does to Jak, as the game's dangerous surfaces: nothing; hurts him (he loses health and is pushed back) or burns him, either of them throwing him up in the air or not; or kills him: an endless fall (the void under a level) or at once. After a death Jak starts again at the last continue point. Only with a collision.
guide.event.example: Example: Burns him and throws him up on a pool of lava; Endless fall on an invisible floor at the bottom of a pit.
guide.levels.title: Levels
guide.levels.text: Every level of your game, by name: Load the level opens it without its creatures; Add to the document puts another one next to it, at its place in the game.
guide.levels.example: Example: open ctyindb (the Industrial Zone), then add its neighbors to see where your changes meet them.
guide.story.title: Story
guide.story.text: The bar at the bottom of the view shows the level at a point of the game: its slider goes through the states of the level, what appears and what goes away.
guide.story.example: Example: see a district before and after the mission that changes it.
guide.replace.title: Replace a level of the game
guide.replace.text: Choose a level of the game this one replaces: exported so, the game loads it in that level's place, at the same coordinates, with its continue points, music and missions. Its original is shown in blue: align yours with it, turn it, or select it whole to move it.
guide.replace.example: Example: a ctyindbis made from ctyindb replaces ctyindb.
guide.export.title: Export for the game
guide.export.text: Writes the level as a custom level of OpenGOAL for Jak 3 (its decor, its collision, its objects and their behaviors) into the library's exports/ folder, with the steps to install it in its README.md.
guide.export.example: Example: export ctyindbis, copy it into your jak-project as its README says, build the game and play it.
guide.demo.select: Click an element to select it
guide.demo.box_select: Drag a box: everything in it is selected
guide.demo.scale: Drag the end of an axis (R)
guide.demo.snap: Snap: by steps of the grid
guide.demo.place: Click in the view to place it, again and again
guide.demo.build: Walls, then a roof, snapped on the grid
guide.demo.build_paint: A material of Jak 3 on the selection
guide.demo.replace: Your level, aligned on the original (blue)
guide.demo.world: World axes: the arrow goes across it
guide.demo.local: Local: the arrow follows its length
guide.demo.free_rotate: Right button held on it: turn it every way
tour.extract.title: Your library and your game
tour.extract.text: The editor works on your own copy of Jak 3: nothing of the game comes with it. At the first start it asks where to keep your library, the folder of everything it makes (File > Settings changes it later). Then File > Extract game assets reads your disc (an .iso file or a folder) once and writes every level into the library, in about a minute and a half; if ogle-extract, the extractor, is missing, the same window offers to download it. Jak II can be extracted too: its structures can then be placed in Jak 3 levels. The tutorial First start goes through it step by step.
tour.levels.title: Open a level
tour.levels.text: The bar of icons on the left opens the panels: Levels (the map, at the top), Build, Catalog, Prefabs and Groups; hover one for its name. Levels lists the levels of the game: choose one, then Load the level (or double-click it). It opens without its creatures, and the inspector on the right shows it. The bar at the bottom of the view shows it at a point of the story, before or after a mission.
tour.camera.title: Look around
tour.camera.text: Hold the right button and fly with WASD (ZQSD on AZERTY); the wheel moves forward. F frames the selection, Home the whole level.
tour.select.title: Select
tour.select.text: Click an element to select it, Shift or Ctrl + click to add more, or drag a box. Click again at the same place to reach what is behind. Ctrl+L selects the whole level.
tour.gizmo.title: Move, turn, stretch
tour.gizmo.text: W, E and R (or Move, Rotate and Scale, at the left of the toolbar) choose the gizmo: drag an arrow to move, a ring to turn, the end of an axis to stretch. The value is shown by the cursor; Shift is ten times finer, and Snap lands on a grid of 0.5 m.
tour.build.title: Build
tour.build.text: The Build panel (the hammer, in the bar on the left) holds walls, floors, roofs, stairs... and the materials of the games. Click a shape, click in the view to place it, then select it and click a texture (choose a level, or search a name).
tour.catalog.title: Place the game's objects
tour.catalog.text: The Catalog has every object of the game but its creatures and collectibles: props, doors and airlocks, water, effects; the interactive ones (platforms, bouncers, crates); its other models; and the decor of every level. Click one, then click in the view.
tour.prefabs.title: Prefabs
tour.prefabs.text: Buildings, houses, bridges, platforms, vents and generators of the game, ready to place; and your own: select elements, then Create a prefab.
tour.behaviors.title: Make the decor act
tour.behaviors.text: Select a piece of decor: the inspector's In the game section sets its collision (its material, deadly, walked through) and whether it throws Jak up (bounce) or sends Jak away (propulsion), as the game's bouncers and vents do.
tour.replace.title: Replace a level of the game
tour.replace.text: Made a ctyindbis from ctyindb? Level > Replace a level of the game: choose ctyindb, show its original (in blue), align your level with it or turn it, select it whole to move it. Exported so, the game loads yours in its place.
tour.export.title: Save and export
tour.export.text: File > Save (Ctrl+S) keeps your level as a project (.glb) in your library. Level > Export for the game writes it as a custom level of OpenGOAL into the library's exports/ folder, with a README.md that gives the steps to build it and play it. Every change can be undone (Ctrl+Z), and an AI assistant can build with you through MCP.
tour.play.title: Into the game
tour.play.text: Level > Export for the game writes your level as files to copy into a jak-project (OpenGOAL's sources), with a README.md giving the exact lines for it. The tutorial Add your level to the game by hand goes through it, up to Jak in your level.
tuto.start.title: Getting started
tuto.move.title: Move
tuto.move.select.title: Select what to move
tuto.move.select.text: Click an element in the view to select it; Shift or Ctrl + click adds one more, a box dragged in the view selects everything inside. Click again at the same place to reach what is behind or under it. The gizmo appears on the selection.
tuto.move.drag.title: Drag an arrow
tuto.move.drag.text: Press W or Move (W) in the toolbar: three arrows, red X, green Y (up), blue Z. Drag an arrow: the selection slides along that axis only, the distance shown next to the cursor. Drag a small square between two arrows to slide in that plane, the middle to follow the cursor.
tuto.move.fine.title: Finer, or by steps
tuto.move.fine.text: While dragging, Shift moves ten times finer, Ctrl goes by the steps of the grid (or frees the move when Snap is on). Snap, in the toolbar, makes every move go by steps (0.5 m by default): pieces line up.
tuto.move.exact.title: Exact values, undo
tuto.move.exact.text: The inspector shows the selection's Position in meters: drag a field or type a value. Ctrl+Z undoes, Ctrl+Y redoes. A piece placed or moved takes the light of the level where it goes.
tuto.rotate.title: Rotate
tuto.rotate.rings.title: Drag a ring
tuto.rotate.rings.text: Press E or Rotate (E): three rings around the selection. Drag a ring to turn it around that axis (red X, green Y the vertical, blue Z); the angle shows next to the cursor.
tuto.rotate.free.title: Turn it freely (right button)
tuto.rotate.free.text: Hold the right button on the selection, or on what you are placing, and move the mouse: it turns on every axis, left-right around the vertical and up-down around the camera's horizontal. Shift is finer; with Snap it turns by steps. Pressed elsewhere, the right button still looks around.
tuto.rotate.exact.title: Exact angles
tuto.rotate.exact.text: The inspector's Rotation, in degrees around X, Y and Z. While placing: R turns by 45 degrees (Shift + R the other way), Ctrl + wheel by 15 degrees.
tuto.scale.title: Scale
tuto.scale.axes.title: Stretch or grow
tuto.scale.axes.text: Press R or Scale (R). Drag the end of an axis: the selection stretches along it; drag the middle: it grows or shrinks in every direction. Each element scales around its own origin.
tuto.scale.exact.title: Exact values
tuto.scale.exact.text: The inspector's Scale; Keep the proportions changes the three together. The game's objects (actors) are drawn at their own size by the game: the inspector says so when one is scaled.
tuto.scale.shapes.title: The editor's shapes
tuto.scale.shapes.text: A shape of the Build panel (wall, floor, stairs...) has a size of its own: after stretching one, Make the scale its size (inspector) keeps its texture's tiling, the bricks staying square.
tuto.local.title: Local axes
tuto.local.what.title: The element's own axes
tuto.local.what.text: By default the gizmo's arrows follow the world's axes (X, Y up, Z), whatever the element's angle. Tick Local in the toolbar: they follow the selected element's own axes, turned with it.
tuto.local.when.title: When to use it
tuto.local.when.text: Local slides a turned piece along its own length (a catwalk set across, a wall at an angle), turns it around its own axis, stretches it along its own sides. Untick it to move things along the level's grid.
tuto.snap.title: Snap
tuto.snap.on.title: By steps
tuto.snap.on.text: Tick Snap in the toolbar: moves go by steps of the grid, turns by steps of angle, scales by steps. Ctrl while dragging does the opposite for that drag (snaps when Snap is off, frees it when it is on).
tuto.snap.steps.title: Its steps
tuto.snap.steps.text: The arrow next to Snap sets them: move (0.5 m by default: the game's walls are 4 m long, its floors on a 0.5 m grid), turn (15 degrees), scale (0.1). Buttons give the usual values.
tuto.snap.place.title: Placing on the grid
tuto.snap.place.text: With Snap on, what you place from the catalog, the prefabs or the Build panel lands on the grid's points: walls and floors line up, side by side.
tuto.game_view.title: Game rendering
tuto.game_view.what.title: The game's own renderer
tuto.game_view.what.text: View > Game rendering (G), on from the start: the level's decor is drawn by the game's own renderer (OpenGOAL's), as the game will show it once exported: its lighting, its fog, its translucent surfaces and decals.
tuto.game_view.hour.title: Sky, hour and weather
tuto.game_view.hour.text: View > Sky, hour and weather... opens a small window: the sky (half a turn around where the camera looks), the hour (a slider, and Dawn, Noon, Dusk, Night; Time passes lets it run), the game's weathers (clear sky, a few clouds, haze, smog, overcast, rain, storm...) or your own with Clouds, Fog / rain and Rain, and Lightning in a storm. It sums up what the game shows: where the sun is and its light, where the fog closes in, whether the lamps of the level are lit (at night).
tuto.game_view.live.title: Edit and see at once
tuto.game_view.live.text: Edit as usual: each change shows at once in the game's rendering (only the part of the level touched is made again). What you place takes the light of the level around it, as it will have in the game.
tuto.game_view.limits.title: What it draws, what it does not
tuto.game_view.limits.text: The decor is drawn by the game's renderer, the game's sky behind it; the objects' models, the particle effects and the moving ocean are drawn by the editor in the game's light and fog, close to it. There are no reflections. G switches to the editor's own view, where every light of the level is on at once: handy to see dark corners.
tuto.ingame.title: In the game: collision, ground, effects
tuto.ingame.section.title: The In the game section
tuto.ingame.section.text: Select an element of the decor (a piece of a level, a shape, a model): the inspector's In the game section says what the game does with it, and the export writes it into the level. Every choice explains itself in its list. Back to the default returns to what the game does on its own.
tuto.ingame.collision.title: Collision: yes or no
tuto.ingame.collision.text: Ticked, Jak stands on the element and bumps into it; unticked, he goes through it. The line under it says the default: the game's own collision for the level's pieces where they are, none for small pieces (under 4 m) and surfaces seen through (water, glass), else one made from its shape. Untick it for foliage, cables, light shafts; tick it for a small crate Jak must climb. Unticked, the choices below are hidden: they need a collision.
tuto.ingame.surface.title: Ground material: the sound of the steps
tuto.ingame.surface.text: What Jak walks on. Mostly the sound of his steps, rolls and landings and the dust they raise: stone, metal, wood, grass, sand, snow... A few change how he moves: Ice (he slides), Gravel (he slides down its slopes), Quicksand (half his speed), Tube (he cannot walk on it), Bottom of water (he is in water). Stop shots: the guns' shots stop on it.
tuto.ingame.event.title: Effect on Jak
tuto.ingame.event.text: What touching the element does to him. Nothing by default. Hurts him (he loses health and is pushed back) or Burns him, either one throwing him up in the air or not. Endless fall (the void under a level) and Kills him at once kill him: he starts again at the last continue point.
tuto.ingame.more.title: More options
tuto.ingame.more.text: Invisible in the game: not drawn, only its collision stays (an invisible wall at the edge of the level). Kind of surface: ground, wall (Jak slides along it) or obstacle; by default its slope decides. And whether Jak can hang from its edges, whether the camera and the creatures go through it, whether enemies see Jak through it.
tuto.ingame.jumps.title: Bounce and propulsion
tuto.ingame.jumps.text: Throws Jak up (bounce): Jak landing on its top is thrown up that height in meters, on foot and on the board. Launches Jak (propulsion): he is sent in an arc to a point (distance, landing height, direction, time in the air). The export writes both as the level's code.
tuto.collision.title: Change the collision face by face
tuto.collision.show.title: See it
tuto.collision.show.text: Open a level and press C (or the toolbar's Collision): its collision is drawn over it, a color per surface, and the Collision window opens. Colors chooses what they tell: the material (the sound of the steps, ice slides), the effect on Jak (hurts, burns, kills) or the kind (ground, wall, obstacle). The legend lists the surfaces and their faces.
tuto.collision.pick.title: Pick faces
tuto.collision.pick.text: Click a face: it turns orange. Shift + click adds one or takes it out; a double click takes the faces of its surface touching it (a whole floor); drag a box for every face whose middle is in it, seen or not; a surface of the legend takes all its faces; Faces under the pieces selected takes those of the pieces you had selected.
tuto.collision.change.title: Change them
tuto.collision.change.text: Their surface: a material, an effect, a kind, then Give it to the faces picked. Delete removes them (Del too): Jak goes through there. Move shows them where they go while you set it, then Move them. Ctrl+Z undoes each change.
tuto.collision.add.title: Add some
tuto.collision.add.text: A click off the collision leaves a yellow cross: A floor or A box adds one there, of the surface chosen (a floor over a hole, an invisible wall at the edge). Collision from the shape of the pieces selected gives pieces faces to change one by one. Where Jak may fall through marks in red the places with more triangles than the game gathers around him.
tuto.materials.title: Materials and textures
tuto.blender.title: Import a model from Blender
tuto.blender.export.title: Export it from Blender
tuto.blender.export.text: In Blender: File > Export > glTF 2.0, format glTF Binary (.glb). Model it in meters (1 unit is 1 meter, Jak is about 1.6 m tall), standing on the ground at the origin. Give its materials an image (Base Color) or a plain color: both come in. Apply its modifiers when exporting.
tuto.blender.import.title: Bring it in
tuto.blender.import.text: Drop the .glb on the editor's window, or File > Import a model. It is copied into the library's models/ folder and follows the cursor: click where it goes. From then on it is in the Catalog's Models, under My models, to place again in any level.
tuto.blender.checks.title: What was checked
tuto.blender.checks.text: Select it: the inspector's Imported model section says its size (a model 100 times too big was made in centimeters), its images, its colors without an image (made into small images: the game would draw them as a checkerboard), its parts and its animations (made with an armature: the Preview plays them; in the game it stays still).
tuto.blender.collision.title: Its collision
tuto.blender.collision.text: A detailed model makes a collision Jak can fall through: the game gathers only about 460 triangles around him. A model you import always collides: by its shape, or, when it is too detailed, by the box around it (12 triangles, solid all around); the check of its collision says which. In the game > Its collision changes it.
tuto.blender.again.title: Change it and bring it in again
tuto.blender.again.text: Edit it in Blender, export it under the same name and import it again: My models gets the new one. What was already placed stays as it was (delete it and place the new one).
tuto.materials.window.title: Game textures...
tuto.materials.window.text: Select a piece: the inspector's Material section lists its materials. Image... gives one an image of your own (PNG, JPG, TGA, BMP); Game textures... opens a window: choose the game (Jak 3, or Jak II when it is extracted), a level (the textures its decor uses), every level or this document, search by name, click a texture.
tuto.materials.catalog.title: For the whole selection
tuto.materials.catalog.text: Catalog > Materials, and the Build panel, give a texture to everything selected at once, all its materials.
tuto.materials.light.title: Its light
tuto.materials.light.text: A piece's color is the game's light, not set by hand: placing or moving a piece gives it the light of the level around it.
tuto.catalog.title: Catalog and Jak II
tuto.catalog.game.title: Choose the game
tuto.catalog.game.text: At the top of the Catalog: the game. Jak 3: its objects (crates, doors, lamps...), its interactive objects, its effects, its models, the decor of its levels, its materials. Jak II (extracted once: Extract Jak II... right there, or File > Extract game assets > Jak II): its objects by their model, its structures and its materials, brought in as decor.
tuto.catalog.objects.title: Place what you chose
tuto.catalog.objects.text: Click a picture, then click in the view to place it, again and again (Esc stops), or drag it into the view. While placing: R and Ctrl + wheel turn it, the right button held turns it every way, Snap puts it on the grid.
tuto.catalog.decor.title: The decor of every level
tuto.catalog.decor.text: Decor shows every piece of every level, or the pieces of one level (the list), searched by name (catwalk, lamp, pillar...). Models and prefabs can be shown by level too. A piece of another level takes the light of the level around it.
tuto.catalog.jak2.title: What comes from Jak II
tuto.catalog.jak2.text: Jak II's pieces, models and prefabs come into a Jak 3 level as decor: their textures are renamed (jak2-...) so as not to mix with Jak 3's, their light is the level's around them, and their objects come without their behavior (Jak II's code is not in Jak 3).
tuto.prefabs.title: Prefabs
tuto.prefabs.game.title: The game's prefabs
tuto.prefabs.game.text: Prefabs > The game's prefabs: assemblies of the decor (houses, bridges, platforms, vents, tanks...) made from your extracted levels, by game (Jak 3, Jak II), level and category. Click one, then place it like an object.
tuto.prefabs.mine.title: Your own prefabs
tuto.prefabs.mine.text: Select elements, then Create a prefab (toolbar, Edit menu or the inspector) and name it: it joins My prefabs, to place in any level. Right-click one to delete it.
tuto.levels.title: Levels and story
tuto.levels.open.title: Open a level
tuto.levels.open.text: Levels panel: choose a level, then Load the level (With its actors: its objects too). Its ground is locked: clicks go to what stands on it (View > Select the ground to change that).
tuto.levels.add.title: Several levels side by side
tuto.levels.add.text: Add to the document puts another level next to it, at its place in the game. The inspector (nothing selected) lists them: show or hide, frame, select a whole level to move it, remove; and the levels around it in the game, to add with a click.
tuto.levels.story.title: The story
tuto.levels.story.text: A level changes along the game: missions add or remove things. The story bar, at the bottom, shows the level at a point of the game; its arrows jump to the next change. Unticked, everything is shown.
tuto.replace.title: Replace a level of the game
tuto.replace.choose.title: Which level
tuto.replace.choose.text: Level > Replace a level of the game: choose the level your work takes the place of. Show the original displays the game's, in blue, to compare with.
tuto.replace.align.title: In its place
tuto.replace.align.text: Place it where the original is puts your level where the game's was (turn it by quarter turns if needed). The continue points of the level replaced say whether Jak lands on ground there.
tuto.replace.export.title: Into the game
tuto.replace.export.text: Export for the game: the game then loads your level in its place, with its continue points, its music, its missions and the levels around it; the README of the export says the one line to change.
tuto.save.title: Save and export
tuto.save.save.title: Save the project
tuto.save.save.text: File > Save (Ctrl+S): the first time, name the project. It goes in the library's projects, a folder of its own: projects/<name>/ with its .glb and, when it has some, its nav meshes for the game. Nothing is saved without you asking: File > Recent projects opens it again.
tuto.save.export.title: Export for the game
tuto.save.export.text: Level > Export for the game writes the level for OpenGOAL in the library's exports/<project>/, laid out like the jak-project folder (custom_assets, goal_src), with a README.md that says how to bring it into the game: the folders to copy, the lines to add, how to build it and go there. Play does it all for you (the tutorial Play your level in the game).
tuto.save.navmesh.title: Where the creatures walk
tuto.save.navmesh.text: Level > Nav meshes: generate where the creatures can walk, around the selection or on the whole level. They are saved with the project and exported with the level.
tuto.first_start.title: First start: library and extraction
tuto.first_start.library.title: Your library
tuto.first_start.library.text: The first time, the editor asks where to keep your library: the folder of the game extracted from your disc (jak3/, jak2/: about 4 GB), your projects (projects/), your levels exported for the game (exports/) and your prefabs (prefabricated/). It suggests Documents/Jak Level Editor (in the OpenGOAL Launcher: jak-level-editor/ in its installation folder, a library of its own); Choose another folder... takes any other, Confirm uses it. File > Settings shows it and changes it later: the new folder is used as it is, nothing is moved nor deleted in the old one.
tuto.first_start.extractor.title: The extractor
tuto.first_start.extractor.text: ogle-extract, the program that reads your disc, comes with the editor's installers and its portable zip. When it is missing, File > Extract game assets says so and, when the application can, offers Download ogle-extract (about 30 MB): the OpenGOAL Launcher gets it so. File > Settings says where it was found.
tuto.first_start.disc.title: Extract your Jak 3
tuto.first_start.disc.text: File > Extract game assets. 1. Your Jak 3 disc: its image (.iso file...) or its folder (Folder...); the editor tells which game and version it is (Jak 3 - ntsc_v1 - SCUS-97330). In the OpenGOAL Launcher, the disc it already extracted is chosen for you. 2. Where to write the levels: your library. 3. Extract all the levels: about a minute and a half for the 272 levels of Jak 3, its progress and its log in the window. The extracted files come from your game: keep them on your computer, do not share them.
tuto.first_start.jak2.title: Jak II, if you like
tuto.first_start.jak2.text: A disc of Jak II is extracted the same way (File > Extract game assets > Jak II), next to Jak 3 (into jak2/): its buildings (Haven City as it was, its palace), its decor, its models and its levels can then be brought into your Jak 3 levels (Jak II at the top of the Levels, Catalog and Prefabs panels); Jak II's own level editing, planned, will read the same files.
tuto.first_start.open.title: Open a level
tuto.first_start.open.text: Once extracted, the Levels panel lists the levels: choose one, then Load the level; or File > New level (Ctrl+N) for an empty one. Extract the game again..., at the bottom of the panel, extracts it once more (after a new version of the editor, or from another disc).
tuto.manual.title: Add your level to the game by hand
tuto.manual.export.title: Export it
tuto.manual.export.text: Level > Export for the game... writes your level into the library's exports/<project>/: its folders custom_assets and goal_src, laid out like jak-project, and a README.md with the exact lines and commands for this level. Keep it open: the next steps follow it.
tuto.manual.jakproject.title: A jak-project to put it in
tuto.manual.jakproject.text: Your levels go into a checkout of jak-project, OpenGOAL's sources: the one of whozghiar/jak-project, whose level builder has the fixes the editor's levels need. Clone it and build it as its README says (goalc, gk and the extractor), then extract and decompile your Jak 3 into it (its iso_data/jak3). This is done once.
tuto.manual.copy.title: Copy the files
tuto.manual.copy.text: Copy the export's custom_assets and goal_src folders into the jak-project folder: they merge with the folders of the same name there. The level has folders of its own (custom_assets/jak3/levels/<name>/): nothing of the game is replaced.
tuto.manual.register.title: Tell the game about it
tuto.manual.register.text: Add the lines the README gives to goal_src/jak3/game.gp, next to the test-zone's. In goal_src/jak3/engine/level/level-info.gc, add the level's definition (the export's level-info.gc) with an :index no other level has; for a level made in place of one of the game's, change that level's :nickname as the README says instead.
tuto.manual.build.title: Build the game
tuto.manual.build.text: Start the compiler (goalc, or task repl in the checkout) and type (mi): it builds the game with your level. Again after each new export of it.
tuto.manual.start.title: Start the game in your level
tuto.manual.start.text: Start gk (gk -g jak3 -- -boot -fakeiso -debug), then in goalc type (lt) and the (start 'play ...) line of the README: the game starts at your level's continue point.
build.no_document: Open a level (Levels panel) or start a new one (File > New level) to build in it.
build.shape.tip: %s, %.1f x %.1f x %.1f m: click, then click in the view to place it, again and again (Esc stops). The inspector changes its size.
build.snap.tip: Moves land on a grid (the steps of Snap, in the toolbar): walls of 4 m meet edge to edge.
build.materials.none: Select shapes or pieces of decor, then click a texture: they all take it.
build.materials.count: A click gives the texture to the %zu selected pieces.
export.note.scripts_dropped: %zu scripts of the game left out ("pair" data: OpenGOAL's level builder cannot write them; the behaviors set in the editor are the level's code): %s
export.note.absent: %zu objects left out: never there (their behavior).
export.note.replace_left_out: %zu elements of the levels next to it left out: the game loads those levels as they are.
export.note.continue_no_ground: %zu continue points of the level replaced have no ground under them (the player would fall): %s
export.note.regions_missing: %zu level replaced without its regions (%s): extract the levels again, or the game will not load the levels around it.
export.note.decor_collision_game: %zu elements with a collision set keep the game's (the levels' own collision covers them): export with the collision made from the decor for it to apply: %s
behavior.title: Behavior
behavior.choose_task: Choose a step of the story...
behavior.task.tip: A step of the story (a task node): true once the player has done it.
behavior.pressed.tip: True once that object was activated: a floor switch pressed (its subtask-complete status).
behavior.gone.tip: True once that object is gone: a crate broken, a pickup taken, an enemy killed (its dead status).
behavior.door.approach.tip: Like the game's doors: it opens when Jak comes near it, and closes behind him.
behavior.door.always.tip: It opens as soon as the level is there, whatever the distance.
behavior.door.when.tip: It opens when Jak comes near it, once the condition below holds.
behavior.door.distance.tip: How near Jak must come for it to open, in meters (-: the game's).
behavior.door.loads.tip: The level behind the door (the rooms of a house, exported as a level of their own): the game loads and shows it when Jak comes to the door, with the levels already there, and opens the door once it is loaded, as its own doors do (the gun course's in the port). Its name, then Enter; empty: none.
behavior.bouncer.height.tip: How high it throws Jak, in meters.
behavior.present.tip: Checked when the level loads: an object not there yet appears the next time the level loads.
params.title: Parameters (%zu)
params.help: What the code of its type reads from the object: the game's values, or the ones set here (x: back to the game's). Distances in meters.
params.list.tip: Numbers separated by spaces; Enter applies.
params.script: script of the game: not exported
preview.title: Preview
preview.none: It does not move: the game does nothing with it but stand there (its effects, if it has some, show in the view: View > Effects).
preview.play.tip: Plays the chosen animation of its model where it stands, as the game plays it (a door opening, a button pushed, a bridge coming down). Nothing of the level changes.
preview.break.tip: Shows it broken: its pieces thrown apart as when Jak breaks it in the game (the pieces the game has for it, else its own model cut up). Nothing of the level changes.
log.preview_mismatch: Preview: the model %s does not match the one in the level
guide.preview.title: Preview an object
guide.preview.text: The interactive objects move in the game: a door opens, a button goes down, an elevator rises, a crate breaks. In the inspector, Preview: Play an animation of its model (the game's), Its movement (what the game's code does with it, imitated: up and down, sliding, turning...), Break it (its pieces thrown apart). It moves where it stands; Stop, or any change to the level, puts it back as it was, and nothing is saved.
preview.motion.rise: The game moves it by its code: up and down, as an elevator or a rising step (imitated here, 8 m). Nothing of the level changes.
preview.motion.fall: The game moves it by its code: it shakes and falls when Jak stands on it (imitated here). Nothing of the level changes.
preview.motion.slide: The game moves it by its code: back and forth along its way (imitated here, 4 m to each side; in the game its path or its settings). Nothing of the level changes.
preview.motion.spin: The game moves it by its code: it turns (imitated here, a turn every 3 s). Nothing of the level changes.
preview.motion.rock: The game moves it by its code: it tilts and floats under Jak's weight (imitated here). Nothing of the level changes.
preview.motion.press: The game moves it by its code: it goes down when Jak presses it (imitated here). Nothing of the level changes.
preview.motion.lift: The game moves it by its code: it opens upwards to let Jak through (imitated here). Nothing of the level changes.
preview.motion.sink: The game moves it by its code: it goes down into the ground to open the way (imitated here). Nothing of the level changes.
preview.motion.bob: The game moves it by its code: it floats and turns slowly (imitated here). Nothing of the level changes.
preview.no_model: The game draws no model of its own for it: what Jak sees of it is part of the level's decor or made of effects (lightning, a vent's blowing, a beam). Its effect shows its picture doing it where it stands.
inspector.shape.step: A step: %.2f m high, %.2f m deep (Size and Steps change them)
inspector.shape.round.tip: Rounds its upright edges: the radius of its corners, in meters (0: square corners). A pillar with a radius of half its width is round.
inspector.shape.bend.tip: Bends it along its width around a vertical axis, in degrees: a wall bent 90 is a quarter of a round tower, 360 a whole one; negative the other way. Its texture follows the curve.
inspector.shape.bend.climb_tip: Bends it along its climb around a vertical axis, in degrees: stairs bent 180 turn half a turn as they rise (a spiral staircase); negative the other way.
build.style: In the style of a level
build.style.none: Its decor has no textured floor nor wall to take.
build.style.floor: Floor: %s, a repeat every %.1f m; ground up and down by %.2f m, bumps %.1f m across
build.style.place_floor.tip: A ground of 16 m by 16 m (the inspector changes its size and bumps), with the floor's texture of this level at its size, its light, and bumps like its ground's. Click in the view to place it.
build.style.place_wall.tip: A wall of 8 m by 4 m with the walls' texture of this level at its size and its light. Click in the view to place it.
guide.style.title: Floors and walls in the style of a level
guide.style.text: Choose a level of the game: the editor measures its decor (the texture its floors draw most and its walls', how large it is there, the light on it, how uneven its ground is). Place a floor gives a ground like its own: the same texture at the same size, the same light, the same bumps (worn and uneven in the slums, flat in the industrial zone); Place a wall a wall of its walls' texture. In the inspector, their size, bumps, bend and corners change as any shape's.
guide.style.example: Example: choose ctysluma, Place a floor, then walls around it: a yard of the slums of Haven City.
inspector.shape.bumps.tip: How far its top goes up and down, in meters (0: flat).
inspector.shape.bump_size.tip: How wide its bumps are, in meters: small for cobbles, large for dunes.
inspector.shape.seed.tip: Another number, other bumps of the same size.
levels.jak2.tip: Jak II: its levels as decor of Jak 3 (extracted once: File > Extract game assets > Jak II). Loaded or added, a level of Jak II brings its decor, its textures renamed jak2-..., and its exact collision (Jak II's surfaces are Jak 3's), without its actors (their code is Jak II's).
levels.jak2.note: Jak II: its decor and its collision, made Jak 3's (no actors).
jak2.missing: Jak II is not extracted yet. Extract it once from your Jak II disc: its levels, models, buildings and materials go into the library's jak2/ folder, where Jak II's own level editing will find them too, without extracting again.
status.topology: Click: a point (or a face) - Shift + click: add - drag: a box - W / E / R: move / turn / scale - Del: delete - T or Esc: done
status.collision: Click: a face of the collision - Shift + click: add - double click: its surface around - drag: a box - Del: delete - C or Esc: done
topology.title: Topology
topology.points.tip: Pick its points (its corners): the vertices at the same place move together, the surface does not tear.
topology.faces.tip: Pick its faces (its triangles): to move, pull out, cut or delete them.
topology.extrude.tip: Pulls the faces picked out by this many meters along their normal, with walls joining them to the rest (a step out of a floor, a pillar out of a wall); negative: pushed in.
topology.subdivide.tip: Cuts each face picked in four: more points to shape it.
topology.flip.tip: Turns the faces picked the other way (their back becomes their front).
topology.delete.tip: Deletes the faces picked (with points: the faces around them). Del does it too.
topology.keys: W / E / R: move, turn, scale what is picked with the gizmo; Ctrl+Z undoes each change.
guide.topology.title: Edit the topology
guide.topology.text: Changes the shape of one element itself: select it, then Topology (T). Its points show over it: click one (Shift adds, a box takes several), then move, turn or scale them with the gizmo (W, E, R); the vertices at the same place move together. Faces picks its triangles: Extrude pulls them out with walls, Subdivide cuts them in four, Flip turns them over, Delete (Del) removes them. T or Esc ends; Ctrl+Z undoes each change. A shape edited so is no longer remade from its size.
guide.topology.example: Example: a floor, Topology, Faces, pick its middle faces and Extrude 2 m: a raised platform out of it.
guide.place_drag.title: Place: raise, lower, slide
guide.place_drag.text: While placing (from the catalog, the prefabs, the Build panel), keep the left button down where it goes and move the mouse: left and right slide it across the view, up and down raise or lower it (Ctrl: forward and back instead), Shift finer, the snap's steps with Snap. It is placed when you let go, and stays selected (a prefab all of it) to be moved again at once.
guide.place_drag.example: Example: a lamp placed on the ground, the button held, the mouse up: it hangs 3 m above the street.
guide.shape_edit.title: Shapes: bend, corners, bumps
guide.shape_edit.text: A shape keeps what it is made of: in the inspector, its size, its steps (stairs), its Bend (degrees around a vertical axis: a wall becomes a curved wall or a round tower, stairs a spiral), its Corners (a box's upright edges rounded) and, for a Ground, its Bumps, their size and variant. Larger or smaller stairs: change their size, the steps follow.
guide.shape_edit.example: Example: a wall of 12 m, Bend 90: a quarter of a round tower; stairs bent 180: a spiral staircase.
guide.jak2_level.title: A level of Jak II
guide.jak2_level.text: In the Levels panel, Levels of: Jak II (its disc extracted once: Extract Jak II...). Load the level opens one of Jak II's levels as a level of Jak 3: its decor (its textures renamed jak2-...), its exact collision (Jak II's surfaces are Jak 3's), without its actors, whose code is Jak II's. Add to the document puts it next to your level. It exports for Jak 3 as any level.
guide.jak2_level.example: Example: Jak II, atoll, Load the level: the atoll of Jak II, to walk in Jak 3.
tuto.place.title: Place an object
tuto.place.click.title: A click places it
tuto.place.click.text: Choose an object in the Catalog (or a prefab, a shape): it follows the cursor, standing on what is under it. A click places it; it is then selected (a prefab all of it), the gizmo on it, to adjust it at once. Hold Shift when you click to go on placing copies; Esc stops.
tuto.place.hold.title: Hold the left button: left, right, up, down
tuto.place.hold.text: Keep the left button down where it goes and move the mouse: left and right slide it across the view, up and down raise or lower it (Ctrl: forward and back instead), a line shows how far. Let go: it is placed there, and stays selected. Shift: finer; with Snap: by its steps.
tuto.place.turn.title: Hold the right button: turn it
tuto.place.turn.text: Keep the right button down and move the mouse: it turns on every axis before it is placed. R (or Ctrl + wheel) turns it around the vertical by 45 degrees.
tuto.topology.title: Edit the topology
tuto.topology.enter.title: Topology mode
