tuto.topology.enter.text: Select one element (a shape, a piece of decor), then Topology (T) in the toolbar: its points show over it, its edges too. The inspector shows how many points and faces it has. T or Esc ends.
tuto.topology.points.title: Move its points
tuto.topology.points.text: Click a point (Shift adds or takes out, a box takes several), then the gizmo: W moves them, E turns them, R scales them around their middle. The vertices at the same place move together: the surface does not tear.
tuto.topology.faces.title: Work its faces
tuto.topology.faces.text: Faces in the inspector: click a face (or a box). Extrude pulls them out by the distance next to it, with walls joining them to the rest; Subdivide cuts each in four (more points to shape); Flip turns them over; Delete (Del) removes them.
tuto.topology.undo.title: Undo, and what changes
tuto.topology.undo.text: Ctrl+Z undoes each change. A shape edited so is no longer remade from its size (its new form is kept as it is), and a piece of decor gets its own mesh: its other copies keep theirs.
tuto.shapes.title: Shapes: size, bend, bumps
tuto.shapes.size.title: Larger, smaller
tuto.shapes.size.text: Place a shape from the Build panel and select it: in the inspector, Size changes its width, height and depth (stairs: their steps follow, the inspector says how high and deep each is), Steps how many; the texture keeps its size.
tuto.shapes.bend.title: Bend it, round it
tuto.shapes.bend.text: Bend curves it around a vertical axis: a wall bent 90 degrees is a quarter of a round tower, 360 a whole one; stairs and ramps bend along their climb (180: a spiral staircase). Corners rounds a box's upright edges: a pillar with a radius of half its width is round.
tuto.shapes.ground.title: A ground with bumps
tuto.shapes.ground.text: Ground (Build panel) is a floor whose top goes up and down: Bumps how much, Bump size how wide (small for cobbles, large for dunes), Variant other bumps of the same size.
tuto.style.title: Floors and walls of a level
tuto.style.choose.title: Choose a level
tuto.style.choose.text: Build panel, In the style of a level: choose a level of the game (type to filter). The editor reads its decor and says what it found: its floors' texture and how many meters a repeat covers, how uneven its ground is, its walls' texture.
tuto.style.floor.title: Place a floor
tuto.style.floor.text: Place a floor: a ground of 16 m by 16 m with that level's floor texture at its size, its light and bumps like its ground's. Click in the view to place it; the inspector changes its size and bumps.
tuto.style.walls.title: Place walls
tuto.style.walls.text: Place a wall: a wall of that level's walls' texture and light. Bend it, round its corners, resize it like any shape.
tuto.preview.title: Preview an object
tuto.preview.play.title: Its animations
tuto.preview.play.text: Place an interactive object of the Catalog (a door, a button, a bridge) and select it: the inspector's Preview lists the animations of its model. Choose one, Play: it moves where it stands, as in the game; Loop plays it again and again.
tuto.preview.motion.title: Its movement
tuto.preview.motion.text: Many objects are moved by the game's code, not by an animation: Its movement imitates it (an elevator goes up and down, a platform slides, a fan turns, a button goes down, a gate opens). Its tooltip says what the game does with it.
tuto.preview.break.title: Break it
tuto.preview.break.text: Crates, fences, walls that Jak breaks: Break it throws their pieces apart (the pieces the game has for them, else their own model cut up). Stop, or any change of the level, puts it back: nothing is saved.
tuto.jak2level.title: Import a level of Jak II
tuto.jak2level.choose.title: Choose it
tuto.jak2level.choose.text: Levels panel, Levels of: Jak II (extract it first when the panel asks: Extract Jak II...). Choose a level, then Load the level (a document of its own) or Add to the document (next to your level).
tuto.jak2level.what.title: What comes
tuto.jak2level.what.text: Its decor, its textures renamed jak2-... (apart from Jak 3's), and its exact collision: Jak II's surfaces are written as Jak 3's. Its actors stay out: their code is Jak II's. In the document it is named jak2-<level>, never taken for a level of Jak 3 of the same name.
tuto.jak2level.export.title: Play it in Jak 3
tuto.jak2level.export.text: Export it for the game as any level: Level > Export for the game writes it with its collision, and its README says how to bring it into Jak 3.
preview.motion.flicker: What it does in the game, shown by its picture: its lightning (or its beam) crackling where it stands. Nothing of the level changes.
preview.motion.blow: What it does in the game, shown by its picture: a vent blowing Jak (and his board) up. Nothing of the level changes.
preview.motion.swing: What it does in the game, shown by its picture: a bar Jak grabs and swings around. Nothing of the level changes.
preview.motion.climb: What it is for in the game: Jak climbs it, up and down (shown by a figure). Nothing of the level changes.
menu.edit.select_assembly.tip: Selects the whole structure the element is part of: what touches it, without the ground (a house with its facades, roof and windows; a bridge with its pillars). To copy it, move it or save it as a prefab.
prefabs.game.being_made: Being made from its level: click to place it once it is made.
status.terrain: Terrain brush: left button: the mode chosen (shown see-through before) - right button held, the mouse up or down: raise or dig - Shift: erase - M: free or magnet brush - Ctrl + wheel or [ ]: its size - B or Esc: end
terrain.title: Terrain brush
terrain.style.title: Level style
terrain.style.tip: The ground painted takes this level's floor texture, its walls and steep slopes its wall texture, with its ground's bumps. Change it between strokes: each part of the terrain keeps the style it was painted with. At first, the style of the level open.
terrain.texture.none: This level's textures are still being read...
terrain.texture.tip: Click to choose among the textures of the level chosen above (the most used first, searched by name): the ground painted takes it (or its walls, slopes and edges), each part of the terrain keeping its own. "The style's": the level's own floor or wall texture.
terrain.style.apply.tip: Gives the whole terrain painted this style's floor and wall textures (Ctrl+Z undoes it). Otherwise, paint over a part to change only it.
terrain.right_button: Right button held: the mouse up raises the ground under the square, down digs it, shown until you let go (back where it started: nothing). Moved sideways: look around.
terrain.free.tip: The square goes where the cursor is, the ground laid at the height where the stroke starts (M: the magnet brush).
terrain.magnet.tip: The square goes where the cursor is, and the ground it lays (or the walls, the ground flattened) keeps the level of the ground already laid beside it: the terrain you are painting, else the top of the decor next to it (a platform, a quay: 2 cm under it). The ground it follows is named next to it, the preview shows it at that level. (M: the free brush.)
terrain.painting: Changing %s (the terrain under the square is the one changed)
terrain.new: A new terrain at the first stroke
terrain.start_new.tip: The next stroke makes another terrain element instead of adding to this one.
terrain.mode.paint.tip: Held down, lays ground under the square at the height where the stroke started, with the relief of the level style (its bumps) and its floor texture; over ground already there, gives it the style chosen. What it lays shows see-through before you click and while you hold the button; it is laid when you let go (Esc: nothing done). Shift erases.
terrain.mode.erase.tip: Held down, takes away the ground and the walls where the square goes: shown in red before you click and while you hold the button, taken away when you let go (Esc: nothing done). Shift paints.
terrain.mode.smooth.tip: Held down, evens the ground under the square: sharp ridges and holes become gentle slopes. Before you click, the ground smoothed shows see-through.
terrain.mode.flatten.tip: Held down, brings the ground under the square to the height where the stroke started: a flat place to build on. Before you click, the ground flattened shows see-through.
terrain.mode.wall.tip: Held down, raises walls where the square goes, as high as set above the ground, upright, with the wall texture of the level style: draw them freehand. They show see-through before you click and while you hold the button, and are raised when you let go (Esc: nothing done). Shift erases.
terrain.size.tip: The side of the square (meters). Ctrl + wheel or [ and ] in the view.
terrain.strength.tip: How fast it smooths or flattens.
terrain.relief.tip: The new ground goes up and down as the level style's ground does (the slums' worn cobbles, the desert's dunes); off: flat.
terrain.cell.tip: The size of the terrain's cells (meters): smaller for finer shapes, larger for wide grounds (fewer triangles). Chosen when the terrain is made.
terrain.generate.tip: Makes natural ground at once over the area around the brush: hills made by a fractal noise, as high as set, smooth or broken, meeting the flat ground at their edges. Its slopes take the wall texture. Then shape them with the brush.
terrain.help: Right button held, the mouse up or down: raises or digs the ground where the square is (it turns green), shown with its height until you let go. Right button moved sideways (or with W A S D): look around. B, Esc or this window's cross: end the brush. Each stroke is undone with Ctrl+Z; the terrain is an element like the others (move it, collision, export).
build.style.terrain.tip: Paints ground freehand with this level's floor (and its walls and slopes with its wall texture), raises and digs it: the terrain brush (B) with this style.
build.structures.intro: Walls, floors and houses made of %s's own pieces, solid on every side. Once placed, change their size: they grow with more of their pieces, never stretched.
build.structures.place.tip: Click in the view where it goes (its box shows where; R turns it). It is one group: a double click selects it, one undo takes it away. Each one is a little different.
route.title: Its route
route.count: %zu points: it goes along them in the game, back and forth.
route.empty: No route yet: it stays where it is (or goes along the game's own route).
route.draw.tip: Then click in the view, point after point (a yellow flag follows the mouse): the route starts where it is and goes through each point clicked, drawn in yellow. Esc stops. Each point is one step to undo.
route.clear.tip: Takes its route away: it goes back to the game's (or stays still).
route.how: A moving platform or an elevator (Catalog, Interactive): select it, then Draw its route in the inspector and click its points in the view.
route.none: This object does not move along a route: choose a moving platform or an elevator.
walk.title: Where creatures walk
walk.made: %zu walkable areas, %d m² (shown in color over the level).
walk.none: Not made yet: the creatures of the level need it.
walk.size.tip: The creatures it is for: small ones go everywhere, large ones keep away from the walls and do not fit under low ceilings.
walk.make: Make it for the whole level
walk.make.tip: The ground creatures of that size can walk on, everywhere in the level, made again from what is there now (a few seconds). The export writes it.
guide.walk.title: Where creatures walk
guide.walk.text: The game's creatures only walk where the level tells them they can: its nav meshes, flat shapes laid over the ground. In the Build panel's Gameplay, choose the size of the creatures (small, Jak's size, large) and Make it for the whole level: the walkable ground shows in color over the level, around the walls and the crates (a large creature keeps further away). Make it again after changing the level. More settings opens the Nav meshes window.
guide.walk.example: Example: a square of the slums with three crates on it: Jak's size, Make it: the square in color, a gap around each crate where a guard could not pass.
guide.route.title: Routes of moving objects
guide.route.text: A moving platform or an elevator goes along a route: points one after the other. Select one (Catalog, Interactive), then in the inspector Draw its route, and click in the view where it goes, point after point: the route starts where it is and shows in yellow. Esc stops. In the game it goes along it and back. Moved, it takes its route with it; Clear the route takes it away.
guide.route.example: Example: a platform at the edge of a gap, Draw its route, a click on the other side, a click higher up on the roof: Jak rides it across and up.
guide.demo.navmesh_walk: A creature walks on it, around the crates
guide.demo.creature_place: A click on the colored ground: an orange flag
guide.demo.creature_walk: In the game, the guard appears there and walks
guide.demo.route: A click per point of its route
guide.demo.route_go: In the game, it goes along it
guide.demo.spawn_start: Jak starts at the blue flag
guide.demo.spawn_fall: Past the green flag, he falls
tuto.playable.title: Make a level playable
tuto.playable.start.title: Where Jak appears
tuto.playable.start.text: The example: a jumping course over the roofs of the slums. Open ctysluma (Levels panel), then in the Build panel, Gameplay, Jak starts here: click on the first roof. A blue flag stands there; the game starts Jak at it, facing the way it faces (R turns it before you click).
tuto.playable.checkpoint.title: A checkpoint halfway
tuto.playable.checkpoint.text: Checkpoint: click on a roof halfway. A green flag: once Jak passed by it, he comes back there instead of at the start when he dies or falls. Put one before each hard jump.
tuto.playable.fall.title: Falling sends him back
tuto.playable.fall.text: Death zone: click in the street under the roofs, then stretch the red box in the inspector so that it covers everything below the course. The game does not draw it: Jak falling into it dies and comes back at his last checkpoint.
tuto.playable.platform.title: A moving platform
tuto.playable.platform.text: Catalog, Interactive: a moving platform (plat). Place it at the edge of a gap between two roofs too far apart to jump.
tuto.playable.route.title: Its route
tuto.playable.route.text: The platform selected, in the inspector: Draw its route. Click on the other side of the gap, then higher up if it should climb: each click is a point of its route, drawn in yellow. Esc stops. In the game, it goes along it and back: Jak rides it across.
tuto.playable.walk.title: Where creatures walk
tuto.playable.walk.text: For the creatures: Build panel, Gameplay, Where creatures walk, Jak's size, Make it for the whole level. The streets and roofs where a guard could walk show in color; the export writes them.
tuto.playable.creature.title: A guard on the way
tuto.playable.creature.text: Gameplay: choose Grunt of the guard, A creature appears here, then click on a roof in color. An orange flag: in the game a guard appears there and walks the colored ground towards Jak. On ground with no color it could not walk: In this level says no ground beside it, and the export leaves it out.
tuto.playable.export.title: Try it in the game
tuto.playable.export.text: File > Export for the game: the start, the checkpoints, the guard, the death zone, the platform's route and the walkable ground are all in the files the export writes. Add them to the game as its README says, and play the course.
tuto.structures.title: Walls and floors that grow
tuto.structures.make.title: Make one
tuto.structures.make.text: Build panel, In the style of a level: choose ctyinda (the industrial zone). Structures like this level's, Make: Wall, Place a solid wall, and click in the view. A solid wall of the zone's metal: pillars and joints standing out of both faces, its bulges, pipes and wear, the same seen from behind.
tuto.structures.grow.title: Make it longer
tuto.structures.grow.text: The wall selected, in the inspector: Length from 24 m to 72 m. It is made again with six more bays between their joints, more bulges and pipes, never stretched; its first bays keep their details. The scale tool (R) does it too when you let go. Another look draws other details.
tuto.structures.set.title: A set of prefabs
tuto.structures.set.text: Make a set of prefabs saves nine structures of the level with your prefabs: walls, a high wall, a wall with windows, floors, houses. Place them from the Prefabs panel, then resize them: they grow the same way.
build.structures.set.tip: Saves with your prefabs nine structures of %s: walls of two and four bays, a high wall, a wall with windows, floors of 16 m and 32 m, houses of 1, 2 and 3 floors. Placed from the Prefabs panel, each grows when you resize it.
build.structures.set_made: %zu prefabs saved: see the Prefabs panel, My prefabs.
structure.text: Made of %s's pieces. Change its size: it is made again with more or fewer of them.
structure.another.tip: The same size and rules, other details: other relief, wear, pipes and lamps where the draw puts them.
structure.grow.tip: The scale tool (R) does it too: let go, it is made again at its new size.
guide.structures.title: Structures that grow
guide.structures.text: Many buildings of the game are only a front, open and flat behind: seen from the other side, they look like a sheet of paper. The editor's structures are solid: a wall has the level's texture on both faces and on its top, pillars and a plinth standing out of both faces, bands between its floors, a coping, and in each bay the level's own relief (the industrial zone's bulges, Spargus' panels), wear, pipes, lamps and beams; a floor is a slab of the level's ground with a curb, the seams of its paving, its dirt patches and vents. Resize one in the inspector, or with the scale tool (R): it is made again with more or fewer of its pieces, never stretched, and its first bays keep their details. Make a set of prefabs saves nine of them for the level.
guide.structures.example: Example: choose ctyinda, Make: Wall, Place a solid wall, then set its length from 24 m to 72 m in the inspector: six more bays between their joints, more bulges and pipes, still the industrial zone's metal on both sides.
menu.edit.history.tip: Every step done, in order: click one to go back to it (or forward again).
menu.edit.repeat.tip: Copies of what is selected in a row, in a circle or scattered around: they show in the view as you choose.
menu.edit.arrange.ground.tip: Each element selected goes down until it rests on what is under it: nothing floats.
menu.edit.arrange.height.tip: Every element selected at the height of the first one clicked (their bottoms level).
menu.edit.arrange.line.tip: From the first one clicked to the farthest, the others evenly spaced on the straight line between them (3 elements or more): a row of lamp posts, of crates.
menu.edit.arrange.face: Facing the way of the first
menu.edit.arrange.face.tip: Every element selected turned the way the first one clicked is.
repeat.title: Repeat the selection
repeat.none: Select something first: the copies are of the selection.
repeat.mode.row.tip: Copies one after the other along X (the red axis) or Z (the blue one): a fence, a row of pillars.
repeat.mode.circle.tip: Copies around a circle the selection is on, each turned with it: columns around a square, a ring of lamps.
repeat.mode.scatter.tip: Copies at random around the selection, on the ground, each turned and sized a little differently: rocks, crates, plants.
repeat.text: %zu copies shown in the view. Keep makes them one step to undo; Cancel or closing takes them away.
history.title: History
history.text: Click a step to go back to just after it; the steps after it stay, greyed, until you change something.
history.start: 0. The document as it was opened
build.gameplay.start.tip: A blue flag: where Jak appears when the level starts, facing the way the flag does. One per level: placing another moves it. The export writes it (a level of its own).
build.gameplay.checkpoint.tip: A green flag: once Jak passes by it, he comes back there when he dies or falls. The export writes each one (a level of its own: a level replacing one of the game's keeps the game's).
build.gameplay.death_zone.tip: A red box the game does not draw: Jak touching it falls to his death and comes back at his last checkpoint. Put it under the level, below the edges he can fall from; stretch it in the inspector.
build.gameplay.creature.tip: An orange flag: where the creature chosen appears when the level is loaded; it walks and attacks Jak from there. It needs ground it can walk on under it: make it below with Where creatures walk (else the export leaves it out). The editor shows the flag, never the creature.
build.gameplay.list.tip: Everything that makes the level playable, to find it again: a click selects it and shows it in the view.
build.gameplay.stranded.tip: No ground in color under this creature: it could not walk, so the export leaves it out. Make the walkable ground (Where creatures walk) or move it onto ground in color.
guide.gameplay.title: Gameplay: start, checkpoints, creatures, death zones
guide.gameplay.text: In the Build panel, Gameplay places what makes a level playable. Jak starts here: a blue flag where Jak appears (one per level). Checkpoint: a green flag; once Jak passes by it, dying or falling brings him back there. Death zone: a red box the game does not draw; Jak falling into it dies and comes back at his last checkpoint. A creature appears here: an orange flag where the creature chosen appears, on ground made with Where creatures walk. In this level lists them all: a click finds one. The flags and the red color are the editor's only: in the game they are invisible. The export writes them into the level's files (its continue points and their code).
guide.gameplay.example: Example: a start on the first platform, a checkpoint halfway, a death zone of 200 m by 200 m below everything: a jumping course that sends Jak back halfway when he misses a jump.
guide.repeat.title: Arrange and repeat
guide.repeat.text: Edit > Arrange puts the selection in order: drop each element onto the ground, set them all at the height of the first, line them up evenly from the first to the farthest, turn them all like the first. Edit > Repeat the selection makes copies in a row, in a circle or scattered around: they show in the view as you change the numbers, Keep makes them one step to undo. Edit > History lists every step: a click goes back to any of them.
guide.repeat.example: Example: one lamp post, Repeat in a row of 8 along X with 6 m between them, Keep: a street lit in a few seconds. A rock, Repeat scattered with 20 copies within 15 m: a rocky field.
export.note.checkpoints_replaced: %zu checkpoints left out: a level replacing one of the game's keeps the game's continue points.
export.note.battle: %zu battles left out: they spawn the game's creatures from its own tables, whose models the level does not have, and the game dies at the first one (place creatures with A creature appears here instead): %s
export.note.needs_level: %zu objects left out: their code needs their own level of the game loaded, by its name, and the game dies without it (replace that level to keep them): %s
export.note.spawn_no_navmesh: %zu creatures left out, no ground they can walk on under them (Build panel, Gameplay: Where creatures walk): %s
guide.terrain.title: Terrain brush
guide.terrain.text: Draws natural ground freehand: Terrain (B) in the toolbar opens the brush and its window (B again, Esc or its cross close it). A square follows the mouse over the level; Ctrl + wheel or [ and ] change its size. Its level style (the open level's at first) gives the ground its floor texture and the walls and slopes its wall texture, cell by cell: change it between strokes to mix grounds. The left button held paints ground, raises walls, erases, smooths or flattens, shown see-through before it is done (Shift: the other way); the free brush lays ground at the height where the stroke starts, the magnet brush (M) at the level of the ground beside it. The right button held and the mouse moved up raises the ground there, down digs it. Generate hills makes natural ground at once. Each stroke is undone with Ctrl+Z.
guide.terrain.example: Example: the style of desert, Paint ground over 60 m, the right button to raise a few dunes and dig a riverbed, Walls around a camp.
guide.assembly.title: Select an assembly
guide.assembly.text: Selects in one go the whole structure an element is part of: what touches it, without the ground (a house of the slums with its facades, roof, windows and what hangs on them; a building of Haven; a bridge with its pillars). Click an element, then Edit > Select its assembly (Ctrl+G) or the inspector's button. In a city everything touches: an assembly wider than 60 m is cut where the fewest elements cross (a street, the seam between two buildings). Then copy it, move it or save it as a prefab.
guide.assembly.example: Example: open the slums, click a wall of a house, Ctrl+G: the house whole; Create a prefab: it can be put in any level.
tuto.terrain.title: Draw a terrain
tuto.terrain.start.title: The brush
tuto.terrain.start.text: Press B (or Terrain (B) in the toolbar): the brush starts and its window opens at the top right of the view. Its level style is the open level's: choose another one in its list (or Terrain brush in this style, in the Build panel) to paint with its floor and wall textures and its bumps. A square follows the mouse over the level; Ctrl + wheel or [ and ] change its size. B again, Esc or the window's cross end it.
tuto.terrain.paint.title: Paint the ground
tuto.terrain.paint.text: Paint ground, then hold the left button and move: ground is laid under the square, shown see-through until you let go (Esc while holding: nothing done). The free brush lays it at the height where the stroke started; the magnet brush (M) at the level of the ground already laid beside the square (the terrain, else the top of the decor next to it). Over ground already there it takes the style chosen: change the style and paint a path, a square, a field. Shift erases. The first stroke makes a terrain element and the next ones add to it (Start a new terrain makes another); to paint it again later, select it, then B.
tuto.terrain.shape.title: Raise, dig, smooth
tuto.terrain.shape.text: Hold the right button and move the mouse up: the ground under the square rises; down: it is dug. The new shape and its height show until you let go (back where it started: nothing; moved sideways first, the right button looks around). With the left button: Smooth turns ridges into slopes, Flatten makes a flat place at the height where the stroke started, Strength sets how fast. Slopes steeper than 45 degrees take the wall texture.
tuto.terrain.walls.title: Walls freehand
tuto.terrain.walls.text: Walls raises upright walls where the square goes, as high as Wall height, with the style's wall texture: draw the walls of a camp, a ruin, a maze. Erase (or Shift) takes ground and walls away, shown in red before it is done.
tuto.terrain.generate.title: Generate hills
tuto.terrain.generate.text: Generate hills, at the bottom of the window: an area, a height, a roughness and a variant, then Generate where the brush is: natural ground at once around the brush. Then shape it with the brush. Each stroke and generation is undone with Ctrl+Z; the terrain exports with its collision like any element.
tuto.assembly.title: A structure as a prefab
tuto.assembly.select.title: Select its assembly
tuto.assembly.select.text: Open a level (the slums, Spargus, Haven of Jak II), click an element of a house: a facade, a window. Then Edit > Select its assembly (Ctrl+G): the whole house is selected, its facades, roof, windows and what hangs on them, without the ground nor the next house.
tuto.assembly.prefab.title: Save it
tuto.assembly.prefab.text: Edit > Create a prefab from the selection..., a name: it is saved with your prefabs (the Prefabs panel) and can be put in any level, copied, turned.
tuto.assembly.game.title: The game's assemblies
tuto.assembly.game.text: The Prefabs tab offers the assemblies of every level of Jak 3 and Jak II found so (houses, buildings, towers, bridges, machines, rock formations), and landmarks taken whole: the palace of Haven on its pillar, its roof, its gardens. They are made from your levels when the panel shows them.
help.editing.11: Ctrl+G: select the whole structure the element is part of (its assembly: a house with its facades, roof and windows)
help.editing.12: B: the terrain brush; hold the left button to paint, raise walls, erase, smooth or flatten; the right button held, the mouse up or down: raise or dig; M: free or magnet brush; Ctrl + wheel or [ ]: its size; Shift: the other way
help.editing.13: Ctrl+N / Ctrl+O / Ctrl+S / Ctrl+Shift+S: a new level, open a project, save, save as; F1: this guide
catalog.effects.help: The visual effects of the game's levels: smoke and steam, fire, lights and neon signs, sparks, water. Each one runs in the view where it is placed (View > Effects), as the game makes it.
guide.effects.title: Catalog: visual effects
guide.effects.text: The particle effects of the game in a category of their own, sorted by kind: smoke and steam, fire, lights, sparks, water. Click one, then click in the view: it runs there as in the game, lit by the hour and lost in the fog far away.
guide.effects.example: Example: steam rising from a vent of the industrial zone, a torch at the door of a temple.
guide.groups.title: Groups
guide.groups.text: Elements kept together under a name. Each prefab you place is one; select elements and press Ctrl+Shift+G to make your own. A double click on one element (or the left button held still on it) selects the whole group; it then moves, turns and copies as one.
guide.groups.example: Example: a market stall made of a counter, an awning and crates, grouped as "stall", copied three times along a street.
cursor.box: %zu elements in the box (Shift: add them, Ctrl: take them out)
cursor.box_remove: - %zu elements taken out of the selection
cursor.select_group: Double click, or hold the button: select it all
cursor.move_delta: Moved x %+.2f  y %+.2f  z %+.2f m (%.2f m)
cursor.moving: Moving: left / right, up / down (Ctrl: forward / back, Shift: finer)
cursor.moving_depth: Moving: left / right, forward / back (Shift: finer)
game.title: Game rendering: sky, hour and weather
game.on: Draw the level as the game does (G)
game.sky_tip: The sky around where the camera looks (half a turn), its horizon and the four directions.
game.hour_tip: The game's time of the day: where the sun is and its color, the ambient light, the sky, the fog, the level's lamps (on at night) and the effects seen only at some hours.
game.time_passes_tip: The hour moves on by itself, as in the game but faster: to watch the light and the sky change.
game.weather_tip: The game's weathers: the clouds dim the sun and grey the light, the fog changes how far one sees and its color, the rain falls around the camera, a storm flashes.

game.rain_tip: Rain falling around the camera (in the game, a level turns it on where it wants it).
game.lightning_tip: With clouds above 0.75: a flash every 5 to 10 seconds lights the level and the sky.
game.effects_tip: The particle effects (steam, sparks, lights): those of the night only at night, all of them lost in the fog far away, as in the game.
game.now_text: The sun is %s, its light %.2f; the fog closes in at %.0f m; the lamps are %s.
weather.clear.tip: No cloud, a clear distance: the full sun.
weather.few_clouds.tip: The weather the game starts with: a sunny sky with a few clouds.
weather.haze.tip: A clear sky, the distance fading sooner in a pale haze.
weather.smog.tip: A clear sky over a thick, colored fog: the city's pollution.
weather.overcast.tip: Clouds over the whole sky: a soft, grey light without shadows of the sun.
weather.overcast_fog.tip: Clouds and fog: the distance is lost.
weather.rain.tip: Overcast, the rain's fog and rain falling.
weather.storm.tip: Dark clouds, a dim light, lightning.
weather.storm_rain.tip: The darkest weather of the game: heavy rain and lightning.
weather.storm_fog.tip: Dark clouds and fog: little can be seen far away.
group.title: Group
group.select_all.tip: Selects every element of the group (a double click on one of them does the same).
group.ungroup.tip: Its elements stay where they are, each one on its own.
group.make.tip: A group keeps elements together under a name: a double click on one selects them all, they move together, the Groups panel lists them. Ctrl+Shift+G.
group.new_text: A name for the group of these %zu elements:
groups.no_document: Open a level or start a new one: its groups are listed here.
groups.help: Elements kept together: each prefab placed [P] and the groups you made [G]. Click: select it. Double click: frame it. Right click: rename it, ungroup it.
groups.none: No group yet. Place a prefab, or select elements and group them (Ctrl+Shift+G).
groups.prefab.tip: A prefab placed: its elements, kept together.
log.prefab_left_out: %zu small elements left out of the prefab
menu.edit.select_group.tip: The prefab placed, or the group, the element is part of: all of it.
menu.view.game_window.tip: The game rendering's settings in a window of their own: its sky (sun, clouds), the hour, the weather, the rain, the lightning.
